claim.why_it_matters: The TOC folio for the UNSTRING statement is transcribed as 766 instead of 769, and the markdown's cross-reference anchor was generated from the wrong number (#page-766). 766 is the folio of 14.9.46 TERMINATE, so following the link lands the reader three pages early, inside the TERMINATE statement, rather than at the start of UNSTRING. The neighbours confirm this is a transcription slip and not an ISO defect: 14.9.47 UNLOCK is 768 and 14.9.49 USE is 774, so 766 breaks the monotonically increasing sequence.

verdict.reasoning: I tried to refute this and could not. (1) Render check: scripts/spec/page_workunit.py 18 at 300 dpi produced E:/Temp/specrecon/v18/spec_p18.png. I cropped the TERMINATE..USE band (box 200,2420-2350,2620) and upscaled 2x to inspect the printed glyphs directly. The digits for 14.9.48 UNSTRING read '769' unambiguously: the third glyph is a 9 with a closed upper bowl and a straight descending tail, visually distinct from the '6' glyphs on the TERMINATE line directly above (open upper stroke, closed lower bowl). The four consecutive printed lines are 14.9.46 TERMINATE 766, 14.9.47 UNLOCK 768, 14.9.48 UNSTRING 769, 14.9.49 USE 774. (2) Quotation check: both quotes are accurate. page-18.md line 44 is byte-for-byte '[14.9.48 UNSTRING statement](#section-14-9-48) <24 U+2026 leaders> [766](#page-766)'. (3) Not-reflow check: the string '769' does not appear anywhere in page-18.md, so the correct folio was not merely displaced to an adjacent line or wrapped. Every other TOC line on the page (765, 766, 768, 774, 780, 785, 796) matches the print exactly; UNSTRING is the sole divergence. (4) Independent corroboration from the spec body, not the render: the UNSTRING section heading at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:32362 ('## 14.9.48 UNSTRING statement') is immediately preceded by the page marker at line 32356, ''. PDF page 799 = printed folio 769 (the front matter contributes a constant +30 offset), so the body itself places UNSTRING on folio 769 and contradicts the TOC line. This is a genuine content discrepancy, not formatting, page-break furniture, or hyphenation. One element of the stated rationale is wrong and is corrected below.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, with the impact clause corrected. The transcription error itself is exactly as claimed: the printed TOC folio for 14.9.48 UNSTRING is 769, and page-18.md line 44 renders it as 766 in both the visible link text and the generated anchor (#page-766). The monotonicity argument holds (UNLOCK 768 < UNSTRING 769 < USE 774; 766 breaks the sequence), and the spec body independently confirms 769 via the <a id="page-799"> marker preceding the '## 14.9.48 UNSTRING statement' heading at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:32362. So this is a transcription slip, not an ISO defect. However, the claim's assertion that the bad link 'lands the reader three pages early, inside the TERMINATE statement' is incorrect. Body anchors in ISO_COBOL.md are numbered by PDF page, while TOC link targets are numbered by printed folio, so every TOC #page-NNN link is systematically off by the +30 front-matter offset. <a id="page-766"> is at line 31088 and heads content in the middle of the 14.9.39 SET statement (FORMAT 8, restricted data-pointer rules), i.e. printed folio ~736 -- not TERMINATE. The correct target for UNSTRING would be #page-799. Two consequences worth recording separately: (a) the folio digit error 769->766 is a real, page-local, correctable defect; (b) it produces a duplicate anchor reference, since line 42 (TERMINATE) and line 44 (UNSTRING) now both point at #page-766, which makes the error mechanically detectable. The broader TOC-anchor offset bug is pre-existing and systemic across the whole contents listing and should be tracked as its own item rather than folded into this one.
